A free public map of global poverty and corruption

Explore any country or territory to see its corruption-perceptions score and rank (Transparency International), its poverty rate (World Bank), and links to the independent accountability organisations and current news reporting covering that country or territory.

This map does not name or describe any individual's corruption case. It shows published, country-level statistics (Transparency International, the World Bank) and links out to independent accountability organisations and current news reporting — Stop Global Poverty does not conduct, publish, or endorse any corruption finding of its own.
This map lists 182 countries and territories, using the same classification as its underlying data sources (Transparency International, the World Bank). A small number of entries — including Taiwan, Kosovo, and Hong Kong — have disputed or distinct political status; their inclusion here reflects that classification and is not a statement by Stop Global Poverty on sovereignty or political recognition.
0 100 CPI score (higher = perceived less corrupt)
